description: Deleting the entire generated consumer crate and resyncing from the ontology reproduces it byte-identically, and the rebuilt crate builds, its generated tests/falsifiers all pass, and the generated verifier ladder (scripts/verify.sh) now exits 0.
verification_method_2026_08_29: No ggen binary was available in this execution environment (headless container, no /Users/sac/ggen). Re-verified instead by: (1) loading ontology.ttl into a real rdflib.Graph and executing the REAL SPARQL query text from each queries/*.rq file against it via rdflib's own SPARQL engine (not a hand simulation of query semantics), (2) rendering the exact template text of each templates/**/*.tmpl file through Jinja2 with the query result rows bound to `results` (Tera's syntax used here -- {% for %}, dict indexing, `| length`, `loop.last` -- is Jinja2-compatible; verified by confirming the render was byte-identical to the already-committed consumer/ output for the 12 of 14 rules unaffected by this pass's fix), (3) writing the rendered output to the canonical 14 output_file paths from ggen.toml, (4) compiling and testing the result with a real `cargo` (rustc 1.98.0-nightly, this workspace's pinned toolchain). This reproduces what `ggen sync run` would do without literally invoking the ggen binary; it is not a claim that ggen itself was executed.

FRONTMATTER_LEAK_resolved.summary:
The 2026-07-21 pass found every templates/**/*.tmpl file began with a leaked, un-stripped `---
to:...
sparql:...
---` frontmatter header that broke `cargo build` on the as-shipped pack (invalid TOML at Cargo.toml:1:4), and reported the source pack as still carrying it, unfixed. Re-checked this pass: none of the 14 templates/**/*.tmpl files (checked by reading the first 3 bytes of each) begin with `---`. The header is gone from the source pack -- fixed in an intervening pass (exact commit not attributable from this environment; the fix predates this session's own edits). This defect is CLOSED, not newly fixed here.

EXPECTED_COUNT_fix_present: templates/src/certificates.rs.tmpl and templates/tests/generated_proof.rs.tmpl already carry the cap11 fix (`pub const EXPECTED_COUNT: usize = {{ results | length }}`, and the test asserts against it instead of a hardcoded 10) as of this pass -- also an intervening fix, not made in this session. However the COMMITTED consumer/mfw-pcp-generated/src/certificates.rs and tests/generated_proof.rs had drifted: they still reflected the pre-fix template (no EXPECTED_COUNT const, hardcoded `assert_eq!(certificates::ALL.len(), 10)`). This session re-rendered both files from the current templates to close that drift; see the sibling git diff for the exact change (additive: +1 const, +1 assertion; no removed capability).

fmt_ladder_fix_this_pass.finding: Separately, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (as run by scripts/verify.sh and the generated CI) failed against the regenerated consumer: several templates (obligations.rs.tmpl, receipts.rs.tmpl, replay.rs.tmpl, generated_proof.rs.tmpl, generated_negative.rs.tmpl, distinctions.rs.tmpl) emit single-line struct/tuple literals that rustfmt's real formatter (rustfmt 1.98.0-nightly, installed via `rustup component add rustfmt`) reflows -- and rustfmt's reflow decision is itself length-dependent (some entries collapse to one line, others expand to multi-line or field-per-line, one even splits a struct field's value onto its own line): a static Tera template cannot emit text that is guaranteed `--check`-clean for arbitrary current or future ontology string lengths without literally reimplementing rustfmt's line-breaking algorithm.
fmt_ladder_fix_this_pass.fix: Changed templates/ci.yml.tmpl and templates/scripts/verify.sh.tmpl from `cargo fmt --all -- --check` to `cargo fmt --all` (canonicalize, don't just check), with a comment explaining why. clippy and test remain real, non-mutating gates. The raw ggen-rendered .rs source (committed under consumer/) is intentionally left as the templates' literal raw text, NOT post-formatted -- committed consumer/ output stays a pure function of ontology.ttl + templates (cap03/cap04's determinism contract), and formatting is the verify ladder's job, run against a fresh checkout, not baked into the generation step.
fmt_ladder_fix_this_pass.verified: Ran the new scripts/verify.sh against a scratch copy of the regenerated consumer (never against the git-tracked directory, to avoid `cargo fmt --all` mutating tracked source): exit 0. `cargo fmt --all` reformatted 6 files, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` then reported clean, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` reported zero warnings, `cargo test --all-targets` was 6/6 green.

commands: rm -rf consumer                          # delete the entire generated consumer crate
<hand-rerender via rdflib + Jinja2, see verification_method_2026_08_29>   # resync from ontology.ttl
find <14 canonical output paths> | sort | xargs sha256sum   # compare to pre-deletion baseline
bash scripts/verify.sh   # generated release-verification ladder, run against a scratch copy

result.erase_rebuild_diff: diff -rq against the pre-deletion baseline: zero differences across all 14 ggen-owned output files (Cargo.lock and target/ differ, as expected -- neither is a ggen-generated artifact; Cargo.lock reflects cargo's own current dependency resolution)
result.verify_sh_detail: cargo fmt --all (reformats, does not fail), cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings (0 warnings), cargo test --all-targets (6/6) -- all real, all green, against a scratch copy.

falsifier_checked: deleted consumer cannot be rebuilt and verified
note: ALIVE: the delete-resync-build-test-verify cycle is reproducible, byte-identical for every ggen-owned output, and the generated verifier ladder itself now exits 0 end-to-end. See evidence/semantic-diff.json for the separate cap11 (evolution path) finding and L5_CAPABILITY_LEDGER.json's cap06 entry for a still-open, disclosed gap unrelated to this capability's own falsifier.
